entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri Vishnu Kumar Srivastava, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Arvind Kumar Pandey, the learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
43 of 2023, under Section 420, 411 I.P.C. and Section 66 of Information of Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, registered at Police Station Bewana, District Ambedkar Nagar.

entities.text: Police Station Bewana, District Ambedkar Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of F.I.R. lodged on 13.04.2023 against three persons, including the applicant, alleging that co-accused Anuj had persuaded the informant to open a bank account and later on the informant came to know that Rs. 7,50,000/- had been deposited in his bank account and the same had been withdrawn and the bank manager told the informant that the amount had been deposited by committing online bank fraud.
It is alleged that Rs 25,000/- used for opening the account were provided by the applicant and co-accused Dhirendra Singh.
Vaibhav Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Vaibhav Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the affidavit filed in support of the bail application, it has been stated that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

The applicant's criminal history has been disclosed in Para 17 of the affidavit, as per which the applicant is involved in Case Crime No.257 of 2022 under Section 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 of POCSCO Act, P.S.- Line Bazar, District Jaunpur, in which he has been granted bail by means of an order dated 23.02.2023.

5. The learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that co-accused Neeraj Prajapati, Suresh Kumar Nishad and Anuj Kumar, have already been granted bail by means of orders dated 04.07.2023, 06.07.2023 and 13.07.2023 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
8243 of 2023, 8384 of 2023 and 8806 of 2023, respectively.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
8243 of 2023, 8384 of 2023 and 8806 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 6. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer of the bail, but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

7. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that besides the present case, the applicant is not involved in any case, including the case of alleged fraud of Rs. 7,50,000/- referred in the F.I.R and that three of the co-accused persons have already been granted bail and without making any observations which may affect the merits of the case, I am of the view that the applicant is also entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Preeti.
